summary: Priority-band cascade during rolling credential refresh causing intermittent 429s for dedicated tenant
description: Customer AtlasSearch reports repeated 429 responses across a subset of their interactive routes during a scheduled rolling credential refresh. Errors began shortly after a control-plane-initiated key rotation for ephemeral session tokens. Requests appear to be accepted by the gateway then rejected with 429 at the rate-limiter during refill windows for the priority (low-latency) lane.
impact: Customer reports elevated error rates for live search and query-autocomplete endpoints affecting ~12% of interactive traffic during the rotation window. No data loss but increased user-facing failures and retries; customer SLAs at risk for the dedicated contract.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated tenant with priority and background lanes configured (priority weight 80, background 20).
2) Schedule a rolling credential refresh of ephemeral credentials across multiple edge ingress hosts.
3) Start 500 concurrent low-latency requests (chat/search) pinned to priority lane while background batch flushers run.
4) Observe transient 429s returned from /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings endpoints around the refresh windows.
observed_logs: [2026-03-10T09:14:23Z] auth-service: rotated ephemeral token set for tenant:atlassearch; propagation-start=09:14:18Z
[2026-03-10T09:14:26Z] api-gateway: incoming request id=abc123 tenant=atlassearch route=/v1/chat/completions auth=ok
[2026-03-10T09:14:26Z] rate-limiter: reject id=abc123 tenant=atlassearch lane=priority reason=token_window_exhausted refill_timer=09:14:30Z
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Rolling credential refresh caused ephemeral session handles to be reclassified briefly which diverted refill credits from the priority lane to a temporary low-priority path, starving priority refill window.

Hypothesis B: Auth-service propagation delay created short-lived token duplication where the rate-limiter counted pre-rotation and post-rotation tokens separately, causing early exhaustion in the computed token bucket for the priority lane.

SRE triage: confirmed correlation between rotation start time and the 429 spike (within 5s). No autoscaler activity was seen. Rate-limiter metrics show a sawtooth drop in priority refill credits while background lane credits spike slightly.

Checked config: tenant had explicit priority-band isolation enabled and a small dedicated burst pool; burst pool shows no exhaustion but weight reallocation logs show 'temporary fallback' events during key refresh.
mitigation: 1) Immediately disabled per-tenant rolling-credential fast-propagation feature for AtlasSearch (control-plane flag) to allow tokens to be refreshed during a quieter window.
2) Applied emergency patch to rate-limiter to treat auth-refresh in-flight markers as neutral (do not reassign refill weight) for 30m window. Patch deployed to canary edge hosts at 09:46Z.
3) Advised customer to stagger background flushers for next rotation and to reduce parallelism of ephemeral-key swap if possible.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied — emergency neutral-marker patch reduced 429 spikes by ~85% in canary and then rolled to remaining us-west hosts. Final fix (refactor of refill accounting to be idempotent during credential transitions) targeted for next minor release. Customer notified and monitoring in place.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-OPS: Implement idempotent refill accounting so rotations do not alter lane weights (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-24).
PRODUCT: Add a 'rotation-friendly' mode in console for dedicated tenants to coordinate credential swaps with rate-limiter maintenance windows (owner: Product infra, due: 2026-04-07).
DOCS: Update runbook 'priority-band-refill-playbook' with credential-rotation checklist and recommended customer steps.
